newsitem.title: UK: Bulgaria takes over Brady market spotlight.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria takes over Brady market spotlight.

text.p: Bulgaria moved into the Brady market spotlight on Tuesday with investors back in after a pause at the end of last week, pushing prices up towards recent highs with more upside potential seen, traders said.
Ecuador was less in demand in early trade than in recent days and dealers said this due to investors taking stock of the uncertainty surrounding the country's presidency.
In London trade focused on Bulgaria's IAB issue which was up about 3/4 point at 54-3/4.

"We think they'll go to 60," said Jerome Booth at ANZ. "Bulgaria is out of line with the rest of the market in terms of spread," he said. "It's doing well this morning...We are still very bullish that the price could come up."
The IAB is the most volatile Bulgarian issue and the one to go for for bullish investors, Booth said. "There's quite a bit of activity. It could last for the next two to four weeks."

In Bulgaria political leaders agreed to speed up privatisation, close loss-making state firms, crack down on corruption and the grey economy and encourage investment, an official statement said on Monday.

"There was a sharp rally at the beginning of last week and some profit-taking later in the week. Yesterday prices started moving up again and are pushing back up towards the highs of last week," another trader said.
In Ecuador the interim president Rosalia Arteaga has refused to hand over power and Congress will hold a key vote to decide who should rule later on Tuesday.
Congress leader Fabia Alarcon has said he will be appointed president at the extraordinary session.
Booth said investors were not too concerned about who would eventually become president as the country has proved its commitment to market reforms and stability.
"I really don't see there's much standing in the way of continued reform in the key areas," he said.
"We see the PDI bond going up to 65 where it was a few weeks ago. There is no real fundamental default risk in Ecuador...it's the only high yield play left in Latin America Bradys."
He said he expected the price to continue edging up a little.
Another trader said he had seen no movement in Ecuador Bradys though the prices looked more or less unchanged.
Russia was also a bit firmer on Tuesday with some funds buying the Russia Vnesh. It was quoted by a trader at 82-3/8.
"This week was always going to be a quiet one. There's the carnival in Brazil today and no data due until Thursday or Friday with a long weekend coming up in the United States," said one trader.
The market was up 0.44 percentage points at 312.98 according to J.P. Morgan's Brady Index.
